## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sippa Sutta* (Ud 3.9; PTS Ud 31) is a short discourse in the *Udāna* of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. According to the SuttaCentral summary, the text offers instruction concerning topics that Buddhist monks should and should not talk about [SuttaCentral]. While modern secondary literature in the dossier does not provide an independent thematic analysis of this discourse, I. B. Horner notes that the *Udāna* commentary (*Paramatthadīpanī* / UdA 205) defines the craft of writing (*lekhā-sippa*) as inscribing syllables in various ways in connection with discussions of worldly crafts not intended for monks [Horner]. Other reference passages in the dossier focus on the generic noun *sippa* ("craft", "art") as an occupational category in early Buddhist social stratification and education rather than examining this sutta directly [Horner].
SuttaCentral identifies verse- and passage-level parallels to the sutta in the *Bhikṣuvarga* (and corresponding Chinese *Śamaṇavarga*) chapters of various *Udānavarga* recensions—including UV 32, UVS 32, Uv Kg 32, T 212.33, and T 213.32—as well as the *Śarīrārthagāthā* [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse computation in DharmaNexus records 177 Pali-internal matches across 29 texts, exhibiting its longest shared passages with other Udāna discourses dealing with inappropriate conversation, notably the *Piṇḍapātika Sutta* (Ud 3.8, §2.25–4.2) and the *Rāja Sutta* (Ud 2.2, §2.25–4.2), as well as conventional conversational framing shared with the *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4), *Dasakanipāta* (AN 10), and *Mahāpadāna Sutta* (DN 14) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated alignments, DharmaNexus detects text reuse between the sutta and the Sanskrit *Bodhasūtra* and the Tibetan translation of the *Brahmajālasūtra* [DharmaNexus].
